feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications/platform leadership, with clear progression, relevant scope, and solid public-sector positioning. It reads polished and substantive, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, and could sharpen impact by foregrounding outcomes over responsibilities.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level narrative: progression within NACo shows increasing leadership, ownership, and technical breadth.  
- Strong credibility through concrete scale indicators: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” “50+ internal publishers,” and named tools/platforms.  
- Writing is professional and mostly error-free, with consistent tone and good alignment to digital strategy, governance, analytics, and multimedia leadership.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition across the header, core competencies, recent projects, and skills sections; several themes recur almost verbatim, which weakens punch and wastes space.  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond scope metrics: include results such as engagement growth, efficiency gains, adoption improvements, campaign performance, or cost savings.  
- Fix minor style inconsistencies: “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s,” mixed list punctuation, and “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia.” “Ranked among the top public universities…” in Education feels unnecessary and less professional than achievements or honors.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it’s slightly dense and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and experience. Tightening it and adding one concrete scale cue would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Consider: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing web platforms, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise website transformation, editorial systems, multimedia production, and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct verbs like “modernizing,” “leading,” or “scaling.”
- Add a concrete scope marker if desired, e.g., “10,000+ page websites” or “multi-channel communications ecosystems,” to increase specificity.
- Keep terminology consistent: use either “web modernization” or “website transformation” across the CV.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; keep it brief here.
- “Governance models/content operations/editorial systems” is strong but somewhat repetitive alongside the subtitle and skills sections.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block largely repeats the header and Topline Skills. It will be more effective if tightened, made more parallel in style, and focused on differentiating strategic strengths rather than restating detailed capabilities.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, parallel noun phrases and remove filler words like “operations” where possible.
- Emphasize highest-value, most recent strengths: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI search, and workflow integration.
- Consider this tighter version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial systems • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Multi-channel communications leadership • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Standardize style: use “and” instead of mixing “&” with longer phrases, unless ampersands are used consistently across the CV.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “AI-enabled…,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “multimedia production” are already prominent in the header.
- This block overlaps heavily with Topline Skills; keep competencies broad here and leave tools/platforms to later sections.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and overlaps with work-experience bullets. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope will make it more impactful as a footer highlight section.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a short lead-in like “Selected Recent Projects” and format each item as a crisp one-liner with parallel structure.
- Replace generic verbs (“Built,” “Developed”) with stronger, more varied phrasing and emphasize platform, audience, or business purpose.
- Trim stacked descriptors: e.g., “hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search, and bill-level AI chat” is strong but could be slightly simplified for readability.
- Consider rewrite: “AI Hybrid Search — Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat to improve policy-content discovery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video work substantially repeat achievements already covered in NACo roles.
- The anniversary campaign may add the most distinct value because it introduces experiential/display work not emphasized elsewhere.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with your NACo director role and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consulting-level outcomes, transformation work, and what is new since returning as a consultant.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on digital strategy, enterprise web improvement, content operations, and AI-enabled member experiences.”
- Replace generic verbs with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Redesigned workflows and analytics for coordinated cross-channel communications” instead of “Build and refine digital systems...”
- Consolidate overlapping web/CMS bullets into one: “Built Drupal campaign experiences, modular microsites, and member toolkits; provided front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for public-facing properties.”
- Add measurable scope where possible: number of sites/pages, users, toolkits, teams supported, time saved, search relevance gains, or adoption metrics for the AI search initiative.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, usability and operational best practices” repeats themes already covered in the Director role; keep only if you can show a new consulting-specific result.
- The microsite and AI search bullets may duplicate Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and let Projects hold the detail.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize enterprise ownership and outcomes, while avoiding overlap with the earlier NACo role’s newsletter/video execution details.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s enterprise digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Recast bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Combine channel oversight into one concise bullet and add measurable results if available: email open/click growth, social engagement, audience growth, production volume, or cost savings.
- Tighten operations/analytics bullets: “Built reporting stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery to improve leadership reporting and decision-making”; “Established governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning systems to improve consistency and speed.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, platform modernization, and systems.
- Video studio bullet may overlap with older video-production bullets; emphasize building organizational capacity, not producing recurring content.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads generic and overlaps with the more senior NACo roles above and below it. Make it more execution-focused, emphasize scale, and show what changed under your leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to stress ownership and scope: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy publishing.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and measurable if possible: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper systems point: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthened editorial planning” and “improved publishing workflows” overlap with governance/operations language in the Director of Digital Media role.
- Weekly video work also overlaps with the earlier Digital Media Manager / Producer entry and footer project list.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. It should sharpen the most senior, differentiating strengths and use tighter phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with 4 concise, higher-signal lines:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows & content operations
- Multi-channel communications leadership across web, email, social & video
- Public-sector advocacy messaging & audience-centered content strategy
- Change “Audience-focused content planning” to “audience-centered content strategy” to sound more senior and less tactical.
- Add “web modernization” because it is a major recent achievement and better reflects current-level impact.
- Keep wording parallel and specific; avoid broad labels like “leadership” without channel or function context.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” already appear in Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is also repeated in the header/Core Competencies; consider varying or consolidating.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill coverage, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes, not repeat a software inventory.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML/CSS/JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Remove lower-priority or dated specifics here, especially “jQuery,” unless it is central to current target roles.
- Put the most relevant/recent strengths first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations.
- If space allows, sharpen impact language: “Enterprise CMS modernization” and “Platform integrations and workflow automation” sound stronger than standalone nouns.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates the “Technical + IT” section; keep this version strategic and let Technical + IT hold the detailed tool list.
- “Workflow automation” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already echo Core Competencies, so avoid repeating identical phrasing.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT.” In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value analytical leadership and decision support rather than repeat software names.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tools-first to capability-first, e.g. “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting and performance optimization.”
- Trim the tool list to the most differentiating platforms: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity.”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with stronger phrasing such as “Executive dashboards and decision support.”
- Consider this rewrite: “Analytics strategy • KPI framework design • Executive dashboards and decision support • GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity • SEO and digital performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Current wording duplicates the “Data, Analytics & Optimization” section almost exactly; Topline Skills should stay more strategic.
- “SEO and performance analysis” may also overlap with broader analytics language; keep only if SEO is a target requirement.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with the Core Competencies line and several NACo bullets. Tighten it to emphasize distinctive production capabilities rather than repeating broad “multimedia” language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, capability-led phrasing:  
  **Video production & post-production • Livestream and webcast production • PTZ camera and studio systems • Hybrid, virtual and in-person event delivery**
- Consider swapping “Studio operations” for a more specific term such as **broadcast studio management** or **control room workflows**.
- If accurate, add scale or complexity in the wording, e.g. **broadcast-quality video production** or **multi-camera livestream production**.
- Keep this section tool/capability-focused; let work experience carry outcomes like studio buildout, recurring programming, and advocacy impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production” and “livestream operations” already appear in Core Competencies; avoid repeating those exact phrases here.
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” partly overlaps with the recent studio/event bullets in Director of Digital Media, so keep this skills line concise and technical.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, scannable list, but it’s generic and slightly redundant with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Since Drupal is the strongest and most recent platform in the work history, this item should reflect that hierarchy.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Add light proficiency framing if space allows: **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If you want more impact, replace the plain list with: **CMS/platforms: Drupal (10,000+ page migration; 3.5M annual page views), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; avoid mixing “web platforms” and “CMS” if some tools are more site-hosting than full CMSs.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider keeping platforms in only one place.
- Drupal already appears repeatedly in recent experience, so this item should stay concise rather than restating implementation details.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize current, hands-on implementation tools and modernize the phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: **Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery • Technical integrations: APIs, Google Tag Manager • Edge/serverless tooling: Cloudflare Workers • Deployment/automation: GitHub Actions**
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless used elsewhere consistently; **HTML, CSS, JavaScript** is cleaner.
- Group skills by function rather than listing flat keywords; this signals practical application, not just familiarity.
- If accurate, add one proof point elsewhere in recent experience, e.g. “built front-end components,” “implemented API-driven features,” or “automated deployments with GitHub Actions.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates **HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations** already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Google Tag Manager” may fit better under **Data, Analytics & Optimization** unless you specifically use it for implementation-heavy tagging.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a pure list to grouped, higher-signal categories: “Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier • Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp • Slack, Teams.”
- If true, add a light qualifier to show applied use: “Workflow automation, project operations and team collaboration tools: …”
- Prioritize the most relevant/recent platforms tied to current work; consider dropping older/lower-value tools like Basecamp or Trello if space is tight.
- If you can support it elsewhere, connect to outcomes indirectly through wording such as “used to support cross-team publishing, approvals and communications workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- Slack/Teams are low-differentiation unless they supported notable operational systems.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Clear but too bare to add much value on its own. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this item should emphasize platform depth and avoid repeating generic “email/newsletters” language.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Tighten platform names for readability/ATS: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add scope qualifiers instead of just listing tools: enterprise email automation, member communications, segmentation, journey orchestration
- Example rewrite: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp | Email automation, audience segmentation, member engagement and campaign delivery

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid adding “newsletters” or “email campaigns” here; that’s already covered in the NACo experience bullets.
- If Higher Logic was the primary platform at NACo, consider ordering it first to better align with recent experience.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and largely duplicates the “Analytics, Insights & Optimization” topline skills and the NACo experience bullets. Tighten it to emphasize methods and decision-making value, not just a repeated tool list.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics, Experimentation & Reporting**
- Replace with: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • KPI design • SEO analysis • Experimentation/A/B testing**
- Drop **Dashboarding** unless you specify a platform or outcome; it reads vague beside Power BI/Looker Studio.
- Order by strongest/recently evidenced tools first: **GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Clarity**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly repeats the “Topline Skills” analytics section; consider making one broader (strategy/outcomes) and this one purely tools/methods.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid overloading both sections with identical phrasing.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to foundational team-building, production, and platform support.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles while helping build NACo’s first in-house digital team and establish workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Split the second sentence into concrete contributions: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and helped expand the organization’s in-house digital content capacity.”
- Tighten the management reference: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised day-to-day work of a digital media associate.”
- Add metrics if available: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, website traffic impact, or turnaround/time-saved from workflow improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this item as launching or establishing the format.
- “strengthening workflows across web, email, social” is echoed in later roles; keep this version foundational, not strategic.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Tighten it to emphasize coordination, innovation support, and the podcast as the clearest distinctive outcome.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout result: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; helped translate project work into digital and multimedia content.”
- Make the podcast achievement a separate clause with stronger action verbs: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Cut vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; specify outputs if possible (e.g., web features, interviews, audio series, stakeholder resources).
- If you can quantify anything, add scale or frequency: number of projects supported, episodes produced, or audiences/stakeholders served.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad “digital content/multimedia production” language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overstate leadership here if later entries show the progression into formal digital leadership.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it reads more like a mixed capability statement than a clean tools entry. It also overlaps with stronger, more recent multimedia leadership already shown in Core Competencies and work experience.

Suggested edit:
- Split software from production capabilities for clarity; keep this item tool-focused.
- Rewrite as: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Podcast editing/production • Livestream production workflows”
- If true, add level or context to strengthen credibility: “broadcast-quality video editing,” “multi-camera livestream production,” or “end-to-end podcast post-production.”
- Consider dropping one lower-value item if space is tight and prioritizing the most current, job-relevant tools.
